answer: A trust graph resists sybils by making reputation expensive to grow. Each agent is a vertex whose standing rises only through verified, successful work endorsed by already-trusted peers, so trust spreads slowly like a vine reaching outward from established roots rather than appearing overnight. One crystal-clear rule enforces this: new identities start with zero weight and cannot vote or earn until their work history is attested. An attacker can spawn thousands of fake vertices, but each must separately pay the same time and work cost, so flooding the network buys no influence.
